recorded_from: cpp/build/v1-ref/record_v1_noquote.exe, linked against the v1 DLL built from ts2python_v1.cpp
derivation: Written by applying contract/semantics.md to the recorded frames by hand.
NOT generated by running any binding.
Recorded from the real v1 DLL, not hand-authored. The v1 source was
checked out from git and built separately; a hand-written v1 fixture would
only restate what we believe v1 looked like, which is the failure mode
gives 2026-04-18T17:31:00Z, matching the DLL's own ts_utc of 1776533460.0.
notes: semantics.md §3.1 says v1 has no way to express 'no quote' and that a
binding reading v1 MUST treat <= 0 as absent. It also said v1_legacy.jsonl
existed for that — but every frame in that file carries 449.99/450.01, so
the rule had ZERO coverage. A binding that skipped the normalisation
passed all ten conformance tests and then read a v1 history replay as a
long run of $0.00 bids. This fixture closes that hole.
Every frame here carries "bid":0.000000 and "ask":0.000000 on the wire.
There is no JSON null anywhere: v1 formats both with a plain %.6f. The
publisher-side normalisation that produces null arrived in v2, and the DLL
shipping inside a user's TradeStation does not update when a binding does.
SPY is the frame that matters. $TICK would be blanked by §3.2 regardless,
so it cannot tell a compliant binding from one that ignores the rule; SPY
is not on the index list and has no such fallback.
No seq or sid on the wire, so expected_messages_lost is null — 'cannot
tell', which is a different claim from 'nothing was lost' (§6.6).
